description: Heinz Reitbauer's glass-fronted landmark in Stadtpark is Vienna's most internationally important restaurant and a benchmark for modern Austrian cuisine. The cooking is precise, deeply regional, and polished without losing the feeling of a grand urban inn. It is the essential affluent-dining reservation in Vienna for guests who want both technical ambition and a sense of place.
highlights: Three-star Austrian fine dining in Stadtpark with iconic modern architecture, elite service, and a world-class wine program.
sources: Michelin Guide; The World's 50 Best Restaurants; 50 Best Discovery; Falstaff; Vienna Tourist Board

description: Juan Amador's destination restaurant brings avant-garde precision to a striking vaulted wine-estate setting in Döbling. The room feels quietly luxurious rather than theatrical, with a tasting-menu format aimed squarely at experienced fine-dining guests. It is Vienna's other three-star heavyweight and a natural choice for a celebratory dinner outside the old center.
highlights: Three-star creative cuisine in the Hajszan Neumann wine estate, with a distinctive vaulted cellar atmosphere.
sources: Michelin Guide; 50 Best Discovery; Falstaff; Gault&Millau; Vienna Tourist Board

description: Konstantin Filippou's flagship is a compact, intensely focused dining room where Austrian, Mediterranean, and seafood-driven ideas meet with fine-dining discipline. The experience is contemporary and confident, with a serious wine program and a room that attracts international gourmets as much as well-informed Viennese regulars. It is one of the city's most reliable two-star special-occasion bookings.
highlights: Two-star city-center tasting menu with Mediterranean freshness, Austrian references, and a polished open-kitchen feel.
sources: Michelin Guide; Falstaff; Gault&Millau; The Times Luxx; Vienna Tourist Board

description: Mraz & Sohn is one of Vienna's most personal fine-dining rooms, run with the imagination and confidence of a long-established culinary family. The surprise-menu format is playful, technically exacting, and more relaxed in tone than many formal two-star restaurants. It is especially strong for diners who want contemporary creativity without hotel-restaurant stiffness.
highlights: Two-star family-run tasting menu in Brigittenau with an inventive surprise format and relaxed luxury energy.
sources: Michelin Guide; Falstaff; Gault&Millau; Vienna Tourist Board

description: Silvio Nickol's restaurant at Palais Coburg is the grand-hotel counterpoint to Vienna's more avant-garde dining rooms. The cuisine is highly composed, product-focused, and supported by one of the city's most serious cellar programs. For affluent travelers who value white-tablecloth ceremony, palace architecture, and polished service, it remains a core Vienna reservation.
highlights: Two-star palace dining with refined modern cuisine, grand architecture, and an exceptional wine-cellar reputation.
sources: Michelin Guide; Falstaff; Gault&Millau; Vienna Tourist Board; The Times Luxx

description: Doubek has quickly become one of Vienna's defining modern fine-dining addresses, with a dark, focused room and cooking that leans into fire, depth, and texture. The menu feels more contemporary and primal than classic Viennese luxury, which makes it a useful contrast to the city's palace and park restaurants. It is a high-priority two-star table for guests looking for a newer-generation Vienna experience.
highlights: Two-star creative restaurant with a fire-led kitchen language and a moody, intimate Josefstadt setting.
sources: Michelin Guide; Falstaff; Gault&Millau; The Times Luxx; Vienna Tourist Board

description: TIAN is Vienna's leading plant-based fine-dining restaurant, treating vegetables, grains, herbs, and dairy alternatives with the seriousness normally reserved for luxury protein. The dining room is calm and polished, with a tasting-menu structure that works well for both committed vegetarians and omnivores seeking a lighter high-end evening. Its Michelin and green-star recognition make it one of the city's essential specialist restaurants.
highlights: Michelin-starred vegetarian tasting menu in the first district, with strong sustainability credentials and elegant service.
sources: Michelin Guide; Falstaff; Gault&Millau; Vienna Tourist Board; Time Out

description: Aend is a sharp, contemporary tasting-menu restaurant that helped push Vienna's serious dining scene beyond old imperial references. The cooking is refined, ingredient-led, and confident, with a room that feels urban rather than grand. It is an excellent choice for diners who want one-star precision with a more modern Austrian mood.
highlights: Michelin-starred contemporary dining in Mariahilf with precise technique and a clean modern aesthetic.
sources: Michelin Guide; Falstaff; Gault&Millau; Vienna Tourist Board

description: Pramerl & the Wolf hides a serious Michelin-starred kitchen behind the informality of a small neighborhood bistro. The room is unshowy, but the cooking is carefully structured and rewardingly precise. It is a strong pick for affluent diners who prefer culinary substance and personality over ceremonial luxury.
highlights: Michelin-starred creative cooking in an intimate Alsergrund bistro setting, known for substance over spectacle.
sources: Michelin Guide; Falstaff; Gault&Millau; Vienna Tourist Board; Time Out

description: Edvard gives the Anantara Palais Hansen a refined fine-dining identity, pairing Mediterranean-influenced modern cooking with a composed Ringstrasse hotel setting. The restaurant suits business dinners and luxury-hotel guests who want a polished evening without leaving the first district. Its Michelin star keeps it firmly in Vienna's top-tier hotel dining set.
highlights: Michelin-starred hotel restaurant on the Ring with refined modern cuisine and discreet service.
sources: Michelin Guide; Falstaff; Gault&Millau; Vienna Tourist Board

description: Glasswing brings Michelin-starred ambition to The Amauris, one of Vienna's most design-conscious luxury hotels. The restaurant balances classic Ringstrasse elegance with a more contemporary visual language and a tasting-menu style suited to international guests. It is a useful new-generation hotel address for affluent diners staying around the Opera and Kärntner Ring.
highlights: Michelin-starred luxury-hotel dining at The Amauris, with a polished Ringstrasse setting and contemporary presentation.
sources: Michelin Guide; Falstaff; Gault&Millau; Vienna Tourist Board; The Times Luxx

description: Apron is a polished Michelin-starred restaurant near Stadtpark with a contemporary Austrian-European menu and a hotel-adjacent sense of control. The cooking is precise and approachable enough for a wide luxury-travel audience. It works especially well for guests who want a formal dinner near the Ring without the scale of the city's three-star temples.
highlights: Michelin-starred modern cuisine close to Stadtpark, with a composed dining room and reliable special-occasion polish.
sources: Michelin Guide; Falstaff; Gault&Millau; Vienna Tourist Board

description: Herzig is a serious one-star restaurant in a less obvious western district, giving Vienna's fine-dining map useful breadth beyond the first district. The cooking is modern, personal, and technically assured, with a setting that feels more destination-neighborhood than grand hotel. It is a strong choice for diners who want to see the city's serious gastronomy away from the usual tourist axis.
highlights: Michelin-starred modern cuisine in Rudolfsheim-Fünfhaus, with a personal chef-driven identity.
sources: Michelin Guide; Falstaff; Gault&Millau; Vienna Tourist Board

description: JOLA is a small vegan fine-dining restaurant that has become one of Vienna's most important specialist tasting-menu addresses. The experience is intimate and carefully controlled, proving that plant-based dining can sit comfortably inside the city's luxury restaurant conversation. Its Michelin and green-star recognition make it a priority for design-conscious and sustainability-minded diners.
highlights: Michelin-starred vegan tasting menu in the first district with a focused, intimate format.
sources: Michelin Guide; Falstaff; Gault&Millau; Vienna Tourist Board; Time Out

description: Addiert gives Vienna a Michelin-starred Korean contemporary chef's-table experience in a compact first-district setting. The format is small, controlled, and highly personal, making it appealing to diners who already know the city's Austrian fine-dining canon. It is one of the most distinctive newer entries in the current Michelin landscape.
highlights: Michelin-starred Korean contemporary chef's table near the Danube Canal, with limited seats and a focused menu.
sources: Michelin Guide; Falstaff; Vienna Tourist Board

description: Esszimmer turns the fashionable Everybody's Darling townhouse into a small-scale fine-dining address with serious culinary intent. The room feels more social and cocktail-adjacent than many star restaurants, but the dinner format remains ambitious enough for Michelin recognition. It is a useful pick for affluent diners who want a stylish evening that does not feel conventionally formal.
highlights: Michelin-starred tasting room inside a fashionable first-district address with cocktails, design, and intimate scale.
sources: Michelin Guide; Falstaff; Gault&Millau; Vienna Tourist Board; The Times Luxx

description: Z'SOM adds a Latin American accent to Vienna's Michelin-starred dining scene, offering a modern tasting-menu approach in Wieden. The restaurant is polished but not overly grand, making it a good option for diners who want international flavor within a serious culinary frame. It broadens the city's luxury dining mix beyond Austrian, French, and Mediterranean idioms.
highlights: Michelin-starred Latin American-influenced modern restaurant in Wieden with a contemporary dinner format.
sources: Michelin Guide; Falstaff; Vienna Tourist Board

description: SHIKI gives Vienna a polished Japanese fine-dining option in the first district, balancing sushi, modern Japanese cooking, and a quietly upscale dining-room atmosphere. It is especially relevant for affluent travelers who want a break from Central European menus while staying within a serious dinner format. The wine, sake, and service standards keep it in the luxury consideration set.
highlights: Premium Japanese dining close to the Opera, with sushi, modern plates, sake, and an elegant first-district room.
sources: Falstaff; Gault&Millau; Michelin Guide; Time Out; Vienna Tourist Board

description: Meierei is the more relaxed Stadtpark sibling to Steirereck, but it remains far more than a casual offshoot. The room and terrace offer a refined way into Viennese classics, cheese culture, and seasonal Austrian cooking with the Reitbauer team's standards behind it. It is one of the best affluent-casual choices when guests want the Steirereck ecosystem without a full three-star evening.
highlights: Relaxed Steirereck sibling with a park terrace, polished Austrian classics, and a serious cheese and wine culture.
sources: The Times Luxx; Michelin Guide; Falstaff; Vienna Tourist Board

description: Das Loft remains Vienna's most obvious skyline dinner address, high above the Danube Canal at SO/ Vienna. The appeal is partly the view, but the modern cuisine, service infrastructure, and affluent hotel setting make it a credible high-end alternative rather than just a bar with food. It is especially useful for visitors seeking design, cocktails, and panorama in one evening.
highlights: Skyline restaurant at SO/ Vienna with panoramic city views, cocktails, and a polished modern dinner offer.
sources: Michelin Guide; Falstaff; Gault&Millau; Time Out; Livingetc

description: Fabios is one of Vienna's defining social dining rooms, combining sleek Italian cooking with a polished first-district crowd. It is less about tasting-menu ambition than about glamour, consistency, and the ability to host a serious business or fashion-world dinner. For affluent locals and repeat visitors, it remains a central luxury-casual address.
highlights: Sleek first-district Italian restaurant with a fashionable crowd, strong service, and a prime city-center address.
sources: Michelin Guide; Falstaff; Gault&Millau; The Times Luxx

description: Zum Schwarzen Kameel is a Viennese institution where the affluent city still meets for wine, canapes, and polished Austrian dining. The formal restaurant side gives the historic deli-and-bar complex enough dinner credibility to sit alongside the city's luxury-casual options. Its location, history, and old-money energy make it culturally indispensable.
highlights: Historic first-district institution with a restaurant, wine culture, delicatessen heritage, and a polished Viennese crowd.
sources: Michelin Guide; Falstaff; Gault&Millau; The Times Luxx; Vienna Tourist Board

description: MAST is one of Vienna's strongest wine-led restaurants, run with the confidence of sommeliers who understand that a serious bottle needs a serious kitchen. The cooking is seasonal and contemporary without losing bistro ease, making it ideal for guests who want a wine-first dinner rather than a formal tasting menu. It is a key modern address for Austria's natural and terroir-driven wine conversation.
highlights: Wine-led modern bistro in Alsergrund with a serious cellar, seasonal plates, and a relaxed affluent crowd.
sources: Michelin Guide; Falstaff; Gault&Millau; Time Out; World of Mouth

description: DiningRuhm brings Nikkei and broader fusion cooking into Vienna's affluent dining market with a polished, energetic format. The restaurant is useful for guests who want something more international and convivial than classic Austrian fine dining. It clears the luxury-casual bar through its service level, beverage offer, and credibility with Vienna's contemporary dining audience.
highlights: Upscale Nikkei and fusion cooking in Wieden with a polished room and strong dinner energy.
sources: Michelin Guide; Falstaff; Gault&Millau; Time Out

description: Reznicek is a modern Austrian restaurant with enough culinary clarity and adult atmosphere to belong in Vienna's high-end casual set. It offers a more grounded counterpoint to the tasting-menu rooms, emphasizing regional character and refined comfort. The appeal is strongest for diners who want a contemporary Beisl feeling without slipping into purely casual territory.
highlights: Modern Austrian cooking in Alsergrund with refined local flavors, wine focus, and polished neighborhood energy.
sources: Michelin Guide; Falstaff; Gault&Millau; Vienna Tourist Board

description: Oak-107 is Vienna's strongest serious grill candidate for diners who want premium meat, smoke, wine, and a more masculine luxury-casual atmosphere. The restaurant has the price point and culinary focus to compete with a special-occasion booking, even without a star. It is a useful archetype in a city otherwise dominated by tasting menus and Viennese classics.
highlights: Premium grill and steak-focused dining in Mariahilf with an affluent dinner format and serious meat program.
sources: Michelin Guide; Falstaff; Gault&Millau

description: Le Salzgries Paris gives Vienna a polished French brasserie alternative in the old center, with seafood, classics, and a room suited to long adult dinners. It is not trying to rival the Michelin tasting-menu restaurants, but it can credibly replace one for a relaxed affluent evening. The appeal lies in mature service, French comfort, and a sense of first-district continuity.
highlights: Classic French brasserie and seafood address in the first district with oysters, mature service, and an adult atmosphere.
sources: Michelin Guide; Falstaff; Gault&Millau; Vienna Tourist Board

description: Vestibül occupies an atmospheric wing of the Burgtheater and remains one of Vienna's most distinctive grand-setting restaurants. The cooking is polished Austrian-European rather than experimental, but the architecture, service, and cultural setting give it real affluent relevance. It is particularly strong before or after an evening in the city center's theatre and museum district.
highlights: Elegant restaurant in the Burgtheater with historic architecture, Austrian-European cooking, and cultural-night appeal.
sources: Michelin Guide; Falstaff; Gault&Millau; Vienna Tourist Board

description: O boufés is Konstantin Filippou's wine-forward, less formal sibling, giving the first district a sharp bistro alternative to full tasting menus. The format is more spontaneous and social, but the culinary lineage and wine focus keep it above ordinary casual dining. It is ideal for affluent diners who want a serious bottle and a precise, modern meal without the full flagship commitment.
highlights: Wine-led bistro from the Konstantin Filippou orbit, with a compact first-district room and serious small-plate cooking.
sources: Michelin Guide; Falstaff; Gault&Millau; Vienna Tourist Board

description: Das Kraus is a modern Leopoldstadt restaurant with a concise, quality-led menu and enough ambition to matter beyond its neighborhood. It offers the kind of confident, adult contemporary cooking that affluent locals use between star bookings. The atmosphere is relaxed, but the sourcing, plating, and wine-minded service give it genuine high-end casual credibility.
highlights: Modern seasonal dining in Leopoldstadt with a relaxed room, serious cooking, and a polished local following.
sources: Michelin Guide; Falstaff; Gault&Millau; Vienna Tourist Board

description: Skopik & Lohn is a chef-loved modern Viennese bistro with enough polish to appeal to luxury travelers on a relaxed night. The painted ceiling, busy room, and confident Austrian-French menu make it feel unmistakably local without being old-fashioned. It is one of the safest informal choices for diners who still care deeply about food and atmosphere.
highlights: Modern Viennese bistro in Leopoldstadt with a famous painted ceiling, strong schnitzel, and off-duty-chef credibility.
sources: Michelin Guide; The Times Luxx; Time Out; Falstaff; Vienna Tourist Board

description: Plachutta Wollzeile is the reference point for Tafelspitz in central Vienna and an essential stop for visitors who want a canonical Viennese meal. It is polished enough for affluent travelers while remaining rooted in the city's beef, broth, and inn traditions. The room can be busy and traditional, but the cultural role is undeniable.
highlights: Central Viennese classic for Tafelspitz, boiled beef service, schnitzel, and a polished traditional dining-room experience.
sources: Vienna Tourist Board; Time Out; Plachutta; Offbeat Budapest; Falstaff

description: Figlmüller is tourist-famous, but the original Wollzeile address still matters as a cultural shorthand for Vienna's schnitzel tradition. The restaurant's appeal is not luxury formality; it is the chance to eat an iconic dish in a historic, tightly run room near St. Stephen's. For a relaxed local-classic quota, it remains more relevant than many technically better but less emblematic taverns.
highlights: Historic schnitzel institution near St. Stephen's Cathedral, known for its signature oversized Viennese-style cutlet.
sources: Figlmüller; Vienna Tourist Board; Time Out; Conde Nast Traveler; Offbeat Budapest

description: Pfarrwirt is one of Vienna's great old dining addresses, set in Heiligenstadt with a deep sense of place and history. The cooking is traditional and comforting, supported by a wine-country atmosphere that feels very different from the Ringstrasse hotel circuit. It is exactly the kind of relaxed but meaningful local dinner an affluent visitor should understand.
highlights: Historic Heiligenstadt inn with classic Viennese cooking, wine-country atmosphere, and deep local character.
sources: The Times Luxx; Vienna Tourist Board; Time Out; Falstaff; Gault&Millau

description: Glacis Beisl is a relaxed Viennese classic tucked behind the MuseumsQuartier, with one of the city's most useful garden settings for a proper dinner. The food stays close to the Beisl tradition but is tidy, seasonal, and accessible to a sophisticated international guest. It rounds out the list as the informal local favorite for a cultural-evening meal near Vienna's museum district.
highlights: Museum-district Beisl with a leafy garden, Viennese comfort dishes, and a relaxed local evening atmosphere.
sources: Time Out; Vienna Tourist Board; Falstaff; Gault&Millau; Wien Mal Anders
